title: It Was Frozen for 24,000 Years. Then It Had Babies

scenes.text: Something frozen for 24,000 years just woke up and had babies.
Scientists drilled it out of Siberian permafrost, three and a half meters down.
It's a bdelloid rotifer, a creature so small you need a microscope to see it.
Radiocarbon dating put that frozen soil at about 24,000 years old, back in the last ice age.
After it thawed, the animal revived and started reproducing, cloning itself.
So an animal that went into the freezer in the ice age is now making copies of itself.

description:
A microscopic animal frozen in Siberian permafrost for about 24,000 years thawed out, came back to life and started cloning itself.
It is a bdelloid rotifer, and the study was published in Current Biology.
What is the oldest thing you would wake up?
first_comment: If you were frozen for 24,000 years, what is the first thing you'd want to see?
